record.title: Mistral releases improved Mistral Large 4 weights with updated coding and cyber claims
record.summary: Mistral says it released an improved Mistral Large 4 checkpoint as open weights on Oct 29, following an Oct 6 public preview and three additional weeks of reinforcement learning. The model card lists a 1.05T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters per token (52B including embeddings and output layers), and the checkpoint is listed on Hugging Face under a modified MIT-style license that requires a separate license for model-as-a-service businesses. Mistral reports updated coding, cybersecurity, finance and browsing results, including 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 47% fewer tokens per task than its stated comparison, and 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index. These are vendor-reported results; the full technical report is not yet available and no independent evaluation or local model run was conducted here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Mistral’s Oct 29 newsroom post announces release of improved Mistral Large 4 weights after an earlier Oct 6 public preview and three additional weeks of reinforcement learning. The linked official Hugging Face checkpoint page is publicly listed; it identifies the checkpoint as mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Mistral reports that Mistral Large 4 scores 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index while using 47% fewer tokens per task than the leading open-weight comparison cited by Mistral; it reports a score of 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 13 percentage points above the public preview with 30% fewer output tokens.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Mistral reports a 51% score on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index and a 96.6% average refusal rate on selected malicious-cyber prompts; the linked model card describes the checkpoint as a 1.05T-total-parameter MoE with 49B active parameters per token (52B including embeddings and output layers).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Mistral says it observed potential uplift for real attacks during monitored live traffic and is modifying its guardrails; it offers a specialized cybersecurity variant to vetted enterprise design partners under contractual safeguards. These are Mistral’s account of its own observations and access policy.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No independent benchmark evaluation, model execution, full training/evaluation report, or production cost measurement was obtained in this review; the reported token reduction does not by itself establish lower wall-clock time, energy use or total cost.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent rerun or audit of the updated coding, cybersecurity, browsing or finance results was inspected.
The public weights are listed but were not downloaded or executed; practical memory, throughput, latency and quality were not measured on real local hardware.
Mistral says a full technical report is forthcoming; the inspected sources do not provide full training, benchmark sampling, prompting or statistical details for the claimed gains.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported performance is borne out, openly downloadable weights for a trillion-parameter multimodal model with claimed stronger coding and defensive-cyber results could materially expand open-model options for capable organizations. The benchmark gains and real-world utility remain first-party claims, and the model is exceptionally large to host.
limitations: All performance and safety metrics in the announcement are reported by Mistral and were not independently reproduced here.
The full technical report is not yet available in the inspected sources.
Token efficiency is not equivalent to lower wall-clock latency, energy use, or total cost.
The 1.05T total-parameter checkpoint has substantial hosting requirements; no local deployment cost was measured.
brief.summary: Mistral says it released an improved Mistral Large 4 checkpoint as open weights on Oct 29, following an Oct 6 public preview and three additional weeks of reinforcement learning. The model card lists a 1.05T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters per token (52B including embeddings and output layers), and the checkpoint is listed on Hugging Face under a modified MIT-style license that requires a separate license for model-as-a-service businesses. Mistral reports updated coding, cybersecurity, finance and browsing results, including 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 47% fewer tokens per task than its stated comparison, and 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index. technical.claimed_result: Mistral reports improved coding, cyber, browsing and finance performance after three additional weeks of reinforcement learning. The article reports 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 47% fewer tokens per task, 41% Terminal-Bench 4.0, 51% Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, 96.6% average refusal on selected malicious-cyber prompts, and 84.5% BrowseComp. These remain vendor-reported metrics.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Oct 29 announcement, official model documentation, and linked public Hugging Face checkpoint page were inspected. The checkpoint is listed for download and documented for vLLM, SGLang and Transformers. No weights were downloaded or executed.
technical.mechanism: The announced update follows community and early-access preview feedback and three weeks of further reinforcement learning. The released model is a multimodal mixture-of-experts checkpoint that unifies instruction, reasoning and agentic capabilities in one set of weights; it supports configurable low, medium and high reasoning modes.
technical.regime: Official model card: 1.05T total parameters, 49B active per token (52B including embeddings/output layers), 128 routed experts with four active per token plus one shared expert, 1M context, and training from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral data centers in Europe. Benchmarks are vendor-reported; detailed protocols, run settings and independent validation were not supplied in the inspected article.
technical.reproducibility: Public checkpoint listed as mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B on Hugging Face with serving guidance for vLLM, SGLang and Transformers. The checkpoint was not downloaded or tested. The modified Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License permits use, modification and commercialization with a separate license requirement for model-as-a-service businesses. A full technical report is forthcoming.
technical.strongest_baseline: For coding-agent efficiency, Mistral reports a 48% Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index score, effectively tied with GLM-5.3, using 47% fewer tokens per task on average. For Terminal-Bench 4.0 it reports 41%, up 13 percentage points versus its public preview with 30% fewer output tokens. These are the vendor’s summaries of benchmark results and are not an independent comparative audit.

brief.title: Mistral releases improved Mistral Large 4 weights with updated coding and cyber claims
brief.why_it_matters: The release makes an improved very large multimodal checkpoint openly downloadable for local deployment and customization, expanding the set of open-weight options for agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity. The article’s benchmark and cost-efficiency claims could make the model relevant to compute and deployment choices if independently confirmed. Its size creates substantial hosting demands, and the current article does not provide a full training/evaluation report or independent validation.
